metadata.title: SECOND ORDER DYNAMICAL SYSTEMS GOVERNED BY MAXIMALLY MONOTONE OPERATORS: QUANTITATIVE STABILITY

items.name: Definition 2.1
items.statement: A single-valued map $A:H\rightarrow H$ is monotone if $\langle Au-Av,u-v\rangle\geq0$ for all $u,v\in H$; $m$-strongly monotone $(m>0)$ if $\langle Au-Av,u-v\rangle\geq m\|u-v\|^2$ for all $u,v\in H$; $\beta$-cocoercive $(\beta>0)$ if $\langle Au-Av,u-v\rangle\geq\beta\|Au-Av\|^2$ for all $u,v\in H$; and $L$-Lipschitz continuous $(L>0)$ if $\|Au-Av\|\leq L\|u-v\|$ for all $u,v\in H$. It is clear that $m\leq L$ and that every $\beta$-cocoercive operator is $\frac1\beta$-Lipschitz continuous. Moreover, every $1$-Lipschitz continuous operator is said to be a contraction.
items.remark: [Foundation: Foundation.Operator.Linear] recall IsMonotone | [Foundation: Foundation.FixedPoint.Nonexpansive] recall CocoerciveOn

items.name: Definition 2.2
items.statement: A function $f:H\to\mathbb R$ is convex if $f(tx+(1-t)y)\leq tf(x)+(1-t)f(y)$ for all $x,y\in H$ and all $t\in[0,1]$; it is $\delta$-strongly convex $(\delta>0)$ if $f(tx+(1-t)y)\leq tf(x)+(1-t)f(y)-\frac\delta2t(1-t)\|x-y\|^2$ for all $x,y\in H$ and all $t\in[0,1]$.
items.remark: [Prove hint: preserve the paper notation and use the listed dependencies.]

items.name: Definition 2.3
items.statement: A function $x:[0,b]\to H$ $(b>0)$ is absolutely continuous if: (i) there exists an integrable $y:[0,b]\to H$ such that $x(t)=x(0)+\int_0^t y(s)ds$ for all $t\in[0,b]$; equivalently (ii) $x$ is continuous and its distributional derivative $\dot x$ is Lebesgue integrable on $[0,b]$; equivalently (iii) for every $\epsilon>0$ there exists $\eta>0$ such that $(I_k\cap I_j=\emptyset\text{ and }\sum_k|b_k-a_k|<\eta)\Rightarrow\sum_k\|f(b_k)-f(a_k)\|<\epsilon$. We call $x:[0,+\infty)\to H$ a strong global solution of $S(A,u_0,v_0)$ if $x$ and $\dot x$ are locally absolutely continuous, $x(0)=u_0$, $\dot x(0)=v_0$, and $\ddot x(t)+\gamma\dot x(t)+Ax(t)=0$ for almost every $t\in[0,+\infty)$.
items.remark: [Prove hint: preserve the paper notation and use the listed dependencies.]

items.name: Lemma 2.6
items.statement: Let $T>0$, $a,b\in L^1(t_0,t_0+T;\mathbb R)$ with $b(t)\geq0$ for a.e. $t\in[t_0,t_0+T]$, $0\leq\alpha<1$, and let $w:[t_0,t_0+T]\to\mathbb R_+$ be absolutely continuous and satisfy $(1-\alpha)w'(t)\leq a(t)w(t)+b(t)w^\alpha(t)$ for a.e. $t\in[t_0,t_0+T]$. Then for all $t\in[t_0,t_0+T]$, $w^{1-\alpha}(t)\leq w^{1-\alpha}(t_0)e^{\int_{t_0}^t a(\tau)d\tau}+\int_{t_0}^t e^{\int_s^t a(\tau)d\tau}b(s)ds.$
items.proof: Cited from: R. E. Showalter, Monotone Operators in Banach Spaces and Nonlinear Partial Differential Equations, Math. Surveys Monogr., 49. American Mathematical Society, Providence, RI, 1997.
items.source: R. E. Showalter, Monotone Operators in Banach Spaces and Nonlinear Partial Differential Equations, Math. Surveys Monogr., 49. American Mathematical Society, Providence, RI, 1997.
items.remark: [Prove hint: preserve the paper notation and use the listed dependencies.]

items.name: Yosida approximation
items.statement: For $\lambda>0$ and a perturbed maximal monotone operator $A(\cdot,\mu):H\times\Lambda\to H$, $A_\lambda(\cdot,\mu)=\frac1\lambda(I-J_\lambda^A(\cdot,\mu))$, where $J_\lambda^A(\cdot,\mu):=(I+\lambda A(\cdot,\mu))^{-1}$ is the resolvent operator of index $\lambda$.
items.remark: [Foundation: Foundation.SetValued.Basic] recall SetValuedOperator.resolvent | [Notation: paper $J_\lambda^A$ is the resolvent and $A_\lambda$ its Yosida approximation]

items.name: $r$-distance $D_r$
items.statement: For $r>0$ and single-valued operators $A,B:H\to H$, $D_r(A,B)=\sup_{u\in B(0,r)}\|Au-Bu\|$.
items.remark: [Prove hint: preserve the paper notation and use the listed dependencies.]

items.name: $d_r$ distance
items.statement: For operators $A,B:H\to H$ and $r>0$, $d_r(A,B):=\sup_{u,v\in B(0,r),u\ne v}\frac{\|Au-Bv\|}{\|u-v\|}$.
items.remark: [Prove hint: preserve the paper notation and use the listed dependencies.]

items.name: Distance, excess, Hausdorff distance, and approximate fixed points
items.statement: For a metric space $X$, $d(x,C):=\inf_{y\in C} d(x,y)$, $e(C,D):=\sup_{x\in C}d(x,D)$, and $h(C,D):=\max\{e(C,D),e(D,C)\}$, with the empty-set conventions in Section 2.2. For $T:X\rightrightarrows X$ and $\varepsilon\geq0$, $\varepsilon\text{-Fix}(T):=\{x\in X:d(x,T(x))\leq\varepsilon\}$ and $\operatorname{Fix}(T):=\{x\in X:x\in T(x)\}$.
items.remark: [Notation: supplies $d$, $e$, $h$, $\operatorname{Fix}$, and $\varepsilon$-Fix used by Theorems 2.4, 2.5, and 7.8]

items.name: Strict contraction
items.statement: A map $T:X\to X$ on a metric space is a contraction if there is $\lambda\in[0,1)$ such that $d(Tx,Ty)\leq\lambda d(x,y)$ for all $x,y\in X$.
items.remark: [Note: Definition 2.1 calls a $1$-Lipschitz map a contraction, whereas Theorems 2.4--2.5 require the strict $\lambda<1$ convention]

items.name: Cauchy--Lipschitz--Picard theorem
items.statement: A globally Lipschitz vector field on a Banach space has a unique global classical solution for each initial value; the paper applies this to the first-order system on $H\times H$.
items.proof: Cited from: A. Haraux, Systèmes Dynamiques Dissipatifs et Applications, Recherches en Mathématiques Appliquées, 17, Masson, Paris, 1991. The paper uses it in Section 2.1 and Theorem 3.1.
items.source: A. Haraux, Systèmes Dynamiques Dissipatifs et Applications, Recherches en Mathématiques Appliquées, 17, Masson, Paris, 1991.
items.remark: [Prove hint: preserve the paper notation and use the listed dependencies.]

items.name: Theorem 2.4
items.statement: Let $X$ be a metric space and let $T_1:X\rightrightarrows X$ and $T_2:X\rightrightarrows X$. Suppose that both $T_1$ and $T_2$ are Lipschitz continuous on $X$ with the same Lipschitz constant $\lambda\in[0,1)$. Then for every $\varepsilon>0$, $\varepsilon$-Fix$(T_i)\neq\emptyset$, $i=1,2$, and $h(\varepsilon\text{-Fix}(T_1),\varepsilon\text{-Fix}(T_2))\leq\frac\varepsilon{1-\lambda}+\frac1{1-\lambda}\sup_{x\in X}h(T_1(x),T_2(x)).$
items.proof: Cited from: M. Ait Mansour, M. A Bahraoui and A. El Bekkali, Metric regularity and Lyusternik-Graves theorem via approximate fixed points of set-valued map in noncomplete metric spaces, Set-Valued Var. Anal., 30 (2022), 233-256.
items.source: M. Ait Mansour, M. A Bahraoui and A. El Bekkali, Metric regularity and Lyusternik-Graves theorem via approximate fixed points of set-valued map in noncomplete metric spaces, Set-Valued Var. Anal., 30 (2022), 233-256.
items.remark: [Prove hint: preserve the paper notation and use the listed dependencies.]

items.name: Theorem 2.5 (Lim's Lemma)
items.statement: Let $X$ be a complete metric space and let $T_1,T_2$ be two maps from $X$ into the family of nonempty closed subsets of $X$. Suppose that both $T_1$ and $T_2$ are Lipschitz continuous on $X$ with the same Lipschitz constant $\lambda\in[0,1)$. Then $h(\operatorname{Fix}(T_1),\operatorname{Fix}(T_2))\leq\frac1{1-\lambda}\sup_{x\in X}h(T_1(x),T_2(x)).$
items.proof: Cited from: T.-C. Lim, On fixed-point stability for set-valued contractive mappings with applications to generalized differential equations, J. Math. Anal. Appl., 110 (1985), 436-441.
items.source: T.-C. Lim, On fixed-point stability for set-valued contractive mappings with applications to generalized differential equations, J. Math. Anal. Appl., 110 (1985), 436-441.
items.remark: [Prove hint: preserve the paper notation and use the listed dependencies.]

items.name: Conditions $(C_1)$ and $(C_2)$
items.statement: $(C_1)$: for each $\mu\in\mathcal V(\bar\mu)$ there exists $\alpha_\mu>0$ such that $\langle A_\mu(u)-A_\mu(v),u-v\rangle\geq\alpha_\mu\|A_\mu(u)-A_\mu(v)\|^2$ for all $u,v\in H$. $(C_2)$: there exist $\theta_1>0$, $\theta_2\in]0,1]$ such that $\|A_\mu(u)-A_{\mu'}(u)\|\leq\theta_1\|\mu-\mu'\|^{\theta_2}$ for all $u\in H$ and $\mu,\mu'\in\mathcal V(\bar\mu)$.
items.remark: [Prove hint: preserve the paper notation and use the listed dependencies.]

items.name: $d_{\lambda,\rho}$ distance
items.statement: For maximal monotone operators $A,B$ and $\lambda,\rho>0$, $d_{\lambda,\rho}(A,B):=\sup_{u\in B(0,\rho)}\|J_\lambda^Au-J_\lambda^Bu\|=\lambda\sup_{u\in B(0,\rho)}\|A_\lambda u-B_\lambda u\|$.
items.remark: [Foundation: Foundation.SetValued.Basic] recall SetValuedOperator.resolvent

items.name: Parametric second-order system
items.statement: For $A_\mu:H\to H$, damping $\gamma>0$, and $(u_0^\mu,v_0^\mu)\in H\times H$, $S(A_\mu,u_0^\mu,v_0^\mu)$ denotes $\ddot x_\mu(t)+\gamma\dot x_\mu(t)+A_\mu(x_\mu(t))=0$ for a.e. $t\geq0$, with $x_\mu(0)=u_0^\mu$ and $\dot x_\mu(0)=v_0^\mu$.
items.remark: [Notation: makes the recurring system label $S(A_\mu,u_0^\mu,v_0^\mu)$ explicit]

items.name: Inertial gradient-like dynamics and parametric minimization
items.statement: $DIN(\varphi,\mu)$ denotes $\ddot x_\mu+\gamma\dot x_\mu+\beta\nabla^2\varphi_\mu(x_\mu)\dot x_\mu+\nabla\varphi_\mu(x_\mu)=0$ with the stated initial data. $(PM_\mu)$ denotes $\min_{x\in H}\varphi(x,\mu)$, and $\arg\min\varphi(\cdot,\mu):=\{x\in H:\varphi(x,\mu)=\inf_{y\in H}\varphi(y,\mu)\}$.
items.remark: [Notation: introduces the DIN and $PM_\mu$ labels and the argmin set used in Section 6]

items.name: Baillon--Haddad theorem
items.statement: For a convex differentiable function with $L$-Lipschitz gradient, its gradient is $1/L$-cocoercive; the paper invokes this as [22, Corollary 18.16] with $L=1/\beta$.
items.proof: Cited from: H. H. Bauschke and P. L. Combettes, Convex Analysis and Monotone Operator Theory in Hilbert Spaces, CMS Books in Mathematics, Springer, New York, 2011, Corollary 18.16.
items.source: H. H. Bauschke and P. L. Combettes, Convex Analysis and Monotone Operator Theory in Hilbert Spaces, CMS Books in Mathematics, Springer, New York, 2011.
items.remark: [Prove hint: preserve the paper notation and use the listed dependencies.]

items.name: Approximate fixed points converge to the exact fixed point
items.statement: For the contractive fixed-point setting used in Section 7, the paper cites [4, Proposition 4(g)] for Painlevé--Kuratowski convergence of $\varepsilon$-approximate fixed points to the unique exact fixed point as $\varepsilon\to0$.
items.proof: Cited from: M. Ait Mansour, M. A. Bahraoui and A. El Bekkali, Metric regularity and Lyusternik-Graves theorem via approximate fixed points of set-valued map in noncomplete metric spaces, Set-Valued Var. Anal., 30 (2022), 233-256, Proposition 4(g).
items.source: M. Ait Mansour, M. A. Bahraoui and A. El Bekkali, Metric regularity and Lyusternik-Graves theorem via approximate fixed points of set-valued map in noncomplete metric spaces, Set-Valued Var. Anal., 30 (2022), 233-256.
items.remark: [Prove hint: preserve the paper notation and use the listed dependencies.]

items.name: Theorem 3.1
items.statement: Assume $(C_1)-(C_2)$. For each $\mu\in\mathcal V(\bar\mu)$ and $(u_0^\mu,v_0^\mu)\in H\times H$, $S(A_\mu,u_0^\mu,v_0^\mu)$ admits a unique strong global solution $x_\mu$ and, if $\mu,\mu'\in\mathcal V(\bar\mu)$, then for a.e. $t\geq0$, $\|x_\mu(t)-x_{\mu'}(t)\|\leq e^{mt}\sqrt{\|u_0^\mu-u_0^{\mu'}\|^2+\|v_0^\mu-v_0^{\mu'}\|^2}+\frac{\theta_1}{m}(e^{mt}-1)\|\mu-\mu'\|^{\theta_2}\tag{3}$, where $m=\max(m_\mu,m_{\mu'})$ and $m_\mu=(1+2\gamma^2+\frac2{\alpha_\mu^2})^{1/2}$.
items.proof: For $X_\mu=(x_\mu,\dot x_\mu)$, write $\dot X_\mu=\mathcal A_\mu(X_\mu)$, $\mathcal A_\mu(u,v)=(v,-\gamma v-A_\mu u)$. Cocoercivity makes $\mathcal A_\mu$ Lipschitz. [Indeed, $\|A_\mu u-A_\mu v\|\leq\alpha_\mu^{-1}\|u-v\|$, and $\|(v-v\prime,-\gamma(v-v\prime)-[A_\mu u-A_\mu u\prime])\|^2\leq(1+2\gamma^2+2/\alpha_\mu^2)\|(u-u\prime,v-v\prime)\|^2$.] For a.e. $t$, $\frac12\frac d{dt}\|X_\mu-X_{\mu'}\|^2\leq m_{\mu'}\|X_\mu-X_{\mu'}\|^2+\theta_1\|\mu-\mu'\|^{\theta_2}\|X_\mu-X_{\mu'}\|$. Applying Lemma 2.6 with $t_0=0$, $\alpha=\frac12$, $a=m_{\mu'}$, $b=\theta_1\|\mu-\mu'\|^{\theta_2}$ and $w=\|X_\mu-X_{\mu'}\|^2$ gives $\|X_\mu(t)-X_{\mu'}(t)\|\leq e^{m_{\mu'}t}\|X_\mu(0)-X_{\mu'}(0)\|+\frac{\theta_1}{m_{\mu'}}(e^{m_{\mu'}t}-1)\|\mu-\mu'\|^{\theta_2}$. Since $\|X_\mu-X_{\mu'}\|\geq\|x_\mu-x_{\mu'}\|$ and $\|X_\mu(0)-X_{\mu'}(0)\|=\sqrt{\|u_0^\mu-u_0^{\mu'}\|^2+\|v_0^\mu-v_0^{\mu'}\|^2}$, symmetry gives (3). [Interchanging $\mu$ and $\mu\prime$ yields the analogous bound with $m_\mu$; replacing both constants by $m=\max(m_\mu,m_{\mu\prime})$ enlarges the right-hand side.]
items.remark: [Prove hint: preserve the paper notation and use the listed dependencies.]

items.name: Theorem 5.4
items.statement: For each $\mu$, let $x_\mu$ be the unique solution of $S(A_\mu,u_0^\mu,v_0^\mu)$. If for given $r,T>0$, $x_\mu(t)\in B(0,r)$ for a.e. $t\in[0,T]$ and every $\mu$, then for a.e. $t\in[0,T]$, $\|x_\mu(t)-x_{\mu'}(t)\|\leq\sqrt{\|u_0^\mu-u_0^{\mu'}\|^2+\|v_0^\mu-v_0^{\mu'}\|^2}\exp\left(2\left(1+2\gamma^2+\frac2{d_r(A_\mu,A_{\mu'})^2}\right)^{1/2}T\right).$
items.proof: For a.e. $t$, $\|A_{\mu'}(x_{\mu'}(t))-A_\mu(x_\mu(t))\|\leq d_r(A_\mu,A_{\mu'})\|x_\mu(t)-x_{\mu'}(t)\|$. Thus $\frac12\frac d{dt}\|X_\mu-X_{\mu'}\|^2\leq(1+2\gamma^2+\frac2{d_r(A_\mu,A_{\mu'})^2})^{1/2}\|X_\mu-X_{\mu'}\|^2$. Integration gives the claimed estimate. [Since $w(t)=\|X_\mu(t)-X_{\mu\prime}(t)\|^2$ satisfies $w\prime(t)\leq2c w(t)$, Gronwall gives $\|X_\mu(t)-X_{\mu\prime}(t)\|\leq e^{ct}\|X_\mu(0)-X_{\mu\prime}(0)\|$; use $t\leq T$ and project onto the first component.]
items.remark: [Prove hint: preserve the paper notation and use the listed dependencies.]

items.name: Theorem 6.1
items.statement: For each $\mu$, let $x_\mu$ be the unique solution of $DIN(\varphi,\mu)$. Assume $\beta\gamma>1$, each $\varphi(\cdot,\mu)$ is differentiable and $\delta_\mu$-strongly convex, and (9). Then for all $\mu,\mu'$ and a.e. $t\geq0$, $\|x_\mu(t)-x_{\mu'}(t)\|\leq e^{-\beta\delta t}\sqrt{\|u_0^\mu-u_0^{\mu'}\|^2+\|v_0^\mu-v_0^{\mu'}\|^2}+\frac{\theta_1}{\delta}(1-e^{-\beta\delta t})\|\mu-\mu'\|^{\theta_2}\tag{17}$, where $\delta=\max(\delta_\mu,\delta_{\mu'})$, $\theta_1=k_1$, and $\theta_2=\gamma_1$.
items.proof:
With $X_\mu=(x_\mu,z_\mu)$, use the equivalent gradient system $\dot X_\mu+
abla\varepsilon_\mu(X_\mu)=0$, where $\varepsilon_\mu(x,z)= eta\varphi_\mu(x)+ rac12\|\sqrt a x+\sqrt b z\|^2$, $a=\gamma- rac1 eta$, $b= rac1 eta$. Assumption (9) gives $\|
abla\varepsilon_\mu(X_\mu)-
abla\varepsilon_{\mu'}(X_\mu)\|\leq eta	heta_1\|\mu-\mu'\|^{	heta_2}$. Strong convexity makes $
abla\varepsilon_{\mu'}$ $ eta\delta_{\mu'}$-strongly monotone, hence $ rac12 rac d{dt}\|X_\mu-X_{\mu'}\|^2\leq- eta\delta_{\mu'}\|X_\mu-X_{\mu'}\|^2+ eta	heta_1\|\mu-\mu'\|^{	heta_2}\|X_\mu-X_{\mu'}\|$. Lemma 2.6 and symmetry yield (17). [Apply Lemma 2.6 to $w=\|X_\mu-X_{\mu\prime}\|^2$ with $a=- eta\delta_{\mu\prime}$ and $b= eta	heta_1\|\mu-\mu\prime\|^{	heta_2}$; the integral is $(1-e^{- eta\delta_{\mu\prime}t})/\delta_{\mu\prime}$.]
items.remark: [Foundation: Foundation.Operator.Linear] recall IsStronglyMonotone | [Prove hint: prove strong monotonicity of $\nabla\varepsilon_\mu$ from strong convexity]

items.name: Definition 6.6
items.statement: For $DIN(\varphi,\mu)$, $\bar x$ is Lyapunov stable for (DIN) if for every $\epsilon>0$ there exists $\delta>0$ such that $\|u_0-\bar x\|<\delta$ implies $\|x(t)-\bar x\|<\epsilon$ for every $t\geq0$; it is asymptotically stable if it is Lyapunov stable and $\|x_0-\bar x\|<\delta$ implies $\lim_{t\to\infty}\|x(t)-\bar x\|=0$. It is Lyapunov uniformly $\bar\mu$-stable for the family if for every $\epsilon>0$ there is $\delta>0$ such that $\|u_0-\bar x\|<\delta$ and $\|\mu-\bar\mu\|<\delta$ imply $\|x_\mu(t)-\bar x\|<\epsilon$ for every $t\geq0$; asymptotic uniform $\bar\mu$-stability additionally requires $\lim_{t\to\infty}\|x_\mu(t)-\bar x\|=0$.
items.remark: [Prove hint: preserve the paper notation and use the listed dependencies.]

items.name: Fixed-point integral map and uniform norm
items.statement: For $T>0$, $\|x\|_\infty:=\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\|x(t)\|$. For a differentiable path $x$, $\Gamma_{A,u_0,v_0}(x)(t):=u_0+t v_0+\int_0^t(s-t)[\gamma\dot x(s)+Ax(s)]\,ds$.
items.remark: [Note: the paper declares $\Gamma$ on $C([0,T];H)$ but its formula uses $\dot x$; formalization needs a $C^1$ or absolutely-continuous path space]

items.name: Alvarez--Attouch--Bolte--Redont Proposition 5.1
items.statement: Under the hypotheses quoted in Section 6, including $\operatorname{int}(\arg\min\varphi)\ne\emptyset$, every trajectory of $(DIN)$ converges strongly to a minimizer of $\varphi$.
items.proof: Cited from: F. Alvarez, H. Attouch, J. Bolte and P. Redont, A second-order gradient-like dissipative dynamical system with hessian-driven damping: Application to optimization and mechanics, J. Math. Pures Appl., 81 (2002), 747-779. The paper uses Proposition 5.1 specifically for strong convergence in Theorem 6.2.
items.source: F. Alvarez, H. Attouch, J. Bolte and P. Redont, A second-order gradient-like dissipative dynamical system with hessian-driven damping: Application to optimization and mechanics, J. Math. Pures Appl., 81 (2002), 747-779.
items.remark: [Prove hint: preserve the paper notation and use the listed dependencies.]

items.name: Remark 3.2
items.statement: If $\alpha_0:=\sup_{\mu\in\mathcal V(\bar\mu)}\alpha_\mu<+\infty$, the conclusion of Theorem 3.1 holds with $m_0=(1+2\gamma^2+\frac2{\alpha_0^2})^{1/2}$. If $(u_0^\mu,v_0^\mu)=(u_0,v_0)$ for all $\mu$, it becomes $\|x_\mu(t)-x_{\mu'}(t)\|\leq\frac{\theta_1}{m}(e^{mt}-1)\|\mu-\mu'\|^{\theta_2}$.
items.remark: [Prove hint: preserve the paper notation and use the listed dependencies.]

items.name: Corollary 4.1
items.statement: Assume each $\varphi(\cdot,\mu)$ is differentiable with $\frac1{\beta_\mu}$-Lipschitz continuous gradient $(\beta_\mu>0)$ and $\|\nabla\varphi(x,\mu)-\nabla\varphi(x,\mu')\|\leq k_1\|\mu-\mu'\|^{\gamma_1}\tag{9}$. Then (8) admits a unique strong global solution $x_\mu$ and $\|x_\mu(t)-x_{\mu'}(t)\|\leq e^{mt}\sqrt{\|u_0^\mu-u_0^{\mu'}\|^2+\|v_0^\mu-v_0^{\mu'}\|^2}+\frac{k_1}{m}(e^{mt}-1)\|\mu-\mu'\|^{\gamma_1}\tag{10}$, where $m=\max(m_\mu,m_{\mu'})$ and $m_\mu=(1+2\gamma^2+\frac2{\beta_\mu^2})^{1/2}$.
items.proof:
Since (8) is $S(A_\mu,u_0^\mu,v_0^\mu)$ with $A(\cdot,\mu)=
abla\varphi(\cdot,\mu)$, use Theorem 3.1. [The Baillon--Haddad step uses the surrounding convexity and differentiability assumptions: $1/ eta_\mu$-Lipschitz continuity of $
abla\varphi_\mu$ gives $ eta_\mu$-cocoercivity, so $(C_1)$ holds with $\alpha_\mu= eta_\mu$.] The Baillon-Haddad Theorem says that $
abla\varphi$ is $ rac1 eta$-Lipschitz iff $\varphi$ is $ eta$-cocoercive; (9) gives $(C_2)$ with $	heta_1=k_1$, $	heta_2=\gamma_1$.
items.remark: [Prove hint: preserve the paper notation and use the listed dependencies.]

items.name: Corollary 4.2
items.statement: Assume $T(\cdot,\mu)$ is a contraction for all $\mu\in\mathcal V(\bar\mu)$ and $\|T(u,\mu)-T(u,\mu')\|\leq\theta_1\|\mu-\mu'\|^{\theta_2}\tag{12}$. Then system (11) admits a unique strong global solution $x_\mu$ and $\|x_\mu(t)-x_{\mu'}(t)\|\leq e^{mt}\sqrt{\|u_0^\mu-u_0^{\mu'}\|^2+\|v_0^\mu-v_0^{\mu'}\|^2}+\frac{\theta_1}{m}(e^{mt}-1)\|\mu-\mu'\|^{\theta_2}$, where $m=(1+2\gamma^2+8)^{1/2}$.
items.proof: For $A_\mu=I-T(\cdot,\mu)$, $\langle A_\mu u-A_\mu v,u-v\rangle-\frac12\|A_\mu u-A_\mu v\|^2=\frac12(\|u-v\|^2-\|T(u,\mu)-T(v,\mu)\|^2)\geq0$. Hence $(C_1)$ holds with $\alpha_\mu=\frac12$; [The displayed identity follows by expanding $\|[u-v]-[T(u,\mu)-T(v,\mu)]\|^2$ and cancelling the cross terms. Since a strict contraction is $1$-Lipschitz, its final nonnegative term proves the cocoercivity inequality.] (12) gives $(C_2)$. Apply Theorem 3.1.
items.remark: [Prove hint: preserve the paper notation and use the listed dependencies.]

items.name: Corollary 4.3
items.statement: Assume that, for all $\lambda>0$, $\|J_\lambda^A(u,\mu)-J_\lambda^A(u,\mu')\|\leq\lambda\theta_1\|\mu-\mu'\|^{\theta_2}\tag{15}$. Then for given $\lambda>0$, system (14) admits a unique strong global solution $x_\mu$ and $\|x_\mu(t)-x_{\mu'}(t)\|\leq e^{mt}\sqrt{\|u_0^\mu-u_0^{\mu'}\|^2+\|v_0^\mu-v_0^{\mu'}\|^2}+\frac{\theta_1}{m}(e^{mt}-1)\|\mu-\mu'\|^{\theta_2}$, where $m=(1+2\gamma^2+\frac2{\lambda^2})^{1/2}$.
items.proof: $A_\lambda(\cdot,\mu)$ is $\frac1\lambda$-Lipschitz and $\lambda$-cocoercive, so $(C_1)$ holds with $\alpha_\mu=\lambda$. [By the resolvent/Yosida properties of a maximal monotone operator, $A_\lambda$ is $\lambda$-cocoercive and therefore $1/\lambda$-Lipschitz.] Assumption (15) implies $\|A_\lambda(u,\mu)-A_\lambda(u,\mu')\|\leq\theta_1\|\mu-\mu'\|^{\theta_2}$, hence $(C_2)$, and (3) applies.
items.remark: [Prove hint: preserve the paper notation and use the listed dependencies.]

items.name: Theorem 5.1
items.statement: For each $\mu$, let $x_\mu$ be the unique solution of $S(A_\mu,u_0^\mu,v_0^\mu)$. Suppose $(C_1)$ and, for given $r,T>0$, $x_\mu(t)\in B(0,r)$ for a.e. $t\in[0,T]$ and every $\mu$. Then, for all $\mu,\mu'$ and a.e. $t\in[0,T]$, $\|x_\mu(t)-x_{\mu'}(t)\|\leq e^{mT}\sqrt{\|u_0^\mu-u_0^{\mu'}\|^2+\|v_0^\mu-v_0^{\mu'}\|^2}+\frac1m(e^{mT}-1)D_r(A_\mu,A_{\mu'})$, where $m=\max(m_\mu,m_{\mu'})$, $m_\mu=(1+2\gamma^2+\frac2{\alpha_\mu^2})^{1/2}$.
items.proof: The proof repeats Theorem 3.1, replacing the $(C_2)$ estimate by $\|\mathcal A_\mu(X_\mu(t))-\mathcal A_{\mu'}(X_\mu(t))\|=\|A_\mu(x_\mu(t))-A_{\mu'}(x_\mu(t))\|\leq D_r(A_\mu,A_{\mu'})$, then applying Lemma 2.6. [With $w=\|X_\mu-X_{\mu\prime}\|^2$, the preceding estimate gives $(1-1/2)w\prime\leq m_{\mu\prime}w+D_r(A_\mu,A_{\mu\prime})w^{1/2}$; Lemma 2.6 therefore yields the stated exponential term after evaluating the constant-coefficient integral.]
items.remark: [Prove hint: preserve the paper notation and use the listed dependencies.]

items.name: Theorem 5.2
items.statement: For given $\lambda>0$, let $x_\mu$ be the unique solution of (14). If for some $\rho,T>0$, $x_\mu(t)\in B(0,\rho)$ for a.e. $t\in[0,T]$, then for all $\mu,\mu'$ and a.e. $t\in[0,T]$, $\|x_\mu(t)-x_{\mu'}(t)\|\leq e^{mT}\sqrt{\|u_0^\mu-u_0^{\mu'}\|^2+\|v_0^\mu-v_0^{\mu'}\|^2}+\frac1{\lambda m}(e^{mT}-1)d_{\lambda,\rho}(A_\mu,A_{\mu'})$, where $m=(1+2\gamma^2+\frac2{\lambda^2})^{1/2}$ and $A_\mu:=A(\cdot,\mu)$.
items.proof: Using $\mathcal A_\mu^\lambda(u,v)=(v,-\gamma v-A_\lambda(u,\mu))$, the $\lambda$-cocoercivity gives $\|\mathcal A_{\mu'}^\lambda(X_\mu)-\mathcal A_{\mu'}^\lambda(X_{\mu'})\|\leq m\|X_\mu-X_{\mu'}\|$, and $\|\mathcal A_\mu^\lambda(X_\mu)-\mathcal A_{\mu'}^\lambda(X_\mu)\|\leq\frac1\lambda d_{\lambda,\rho}(A_\mu,A_{\mu'})$. Lemma 2.6 yields the asserted estimate. [More explicitly, use $d_{\lambda,\rho}=\lambda\sup_{u\in B(0,\rho)}\|A_\lambda u-B_\lambda u\|$ and the trajectory containment to obtain the forcing coefficient $d_{\lambda,\rho}/\lambda$, then evaluate Lemma 2.6 with $\alpha=1/2$.]
items.remark: [Prove hint: preserve the paper notation and use the listed dependencies.]

items.name: Theorem 6.2
items.statement: For each $\mu$, let $x_\mu$ be the unique solution of $DIN(\varphi,\mu)$ and suppose $\arg\min\varphi(\cdot,\mu)\ne\emptyset$. Under the hypotheses of Theorem 6.1 and $\operatorname{int}(\arg\min\varphi(\cdot,\mu))\ne\emptyset$, $(x_\mu(t))_{t\geq0}$ converges strongly to the unique solution $\bar x_\mu$ of $(PM_\mu)$, and $\|\bar x_\mu-\bar x_{\mu'}\|\leq\frac{\theta_1}{\delta}\|\mu-\mu'\|^{\theta_2}\tag{23}$ for $\delta=\max(\delta_\mu,\delta_{\mu'})$.
items.proof: Uniqueness follows from strong convexity; strong convergence follows from [10, Proposition 5.1]. [The cited proposition supplies $x_\mu(t)\to\bar x_\mu$ and $x_{\mu\prime}(t)\to\bar x_{\mu\prime}$ strongly, while $e^{-\beta\delta t}\to0$ and $1-e^{-\beta\delta t}\to1.] Passing to the limit $t\to+\infty$ in (17) gives $\|\bar x_\mu-\bar x_{\mu'}\|\leq\frac{\theta_1}{\delta}\|\mu-\mu'\|^{\theta_2}$.
items.remark: [Prove hint: apply the external convergence result, then take limits in Theorem 6.1]

If, instead of (9), for given $r,T>0$, $x_\mu(t)\in B(0,r)$ for a.e. $t\in[0,T]$ and all $\mu$, then $\|
abla\varepsilon_\mu(X_\mu(t))-
abla\varepsilon_{\mu'}(X_\mu(t))\|\leq eta D_r(
abla\varphi_\mu,
abla\varphi_{\mu'}).$

items.name: Theorem 6.7
items.statement: Assume the conditions of Theorem 6.1 and that $\bar x$ is Lyapunov stable for (DIN). (i) If $\lim_{\mu\to\bar\mu}(u_0^\mu,v_0^\mu)=(u_0,v_0)$, then $\bar x$ is Lyapunov uniformly $\bar\mu$-stable for $DIN(\varphi,\mu)$. (ii) If moreover $(u_0^\mu,v_0^\mu)=(u_0,v_0)$ for all $\mu$, then $\bar x$ is asymptotically uniformly $\bar\mu$-stable.
items.proof: For $\epsilon>0$, Lyapunov stability supplies $\delta_0$ with $\|x(t)-\bar x\|<\epsilon/3$. Initial-data convergence supplies $\delta_1$ with $\|(u_0^\mu,v_0^\mu)-(u_0,v_0)\|<\epsilon/3$. Using (17), $\|x_\mu(t)-\bar x\|\leq\|(u_0^\mu,v_0^\mu)-(u_0,v_0)\|+\frac{\theta_1}{\delta}\|\mu-\bar\mu\|^{\theta_2}+\|x(t)-\bar x\|<\epsilon$. Under equal initial data, the limiting version of this inequality gives the stated asymptotic conclusion. [TODO: verify: with fixed $\mu\ne\bar\mu$, the displayed estimate leaves the positive term $(\theta_1/\delta)\|\mu-\bar\mu\|^{\theta_2}$ as $t\to\infty$, so it does not prove convergence to $\bar x$ without an additional argument or $\mu=\bar\mu$.]
items.remark: [Prove hint: preserve the paper notation and use the listed dependencies.]

items.name: Theorem 7.1
items.statement: Assume for some $\alpha>0$ that $A_\mu$ is $\alpha$-cocoercive for each $\mu\in\mathcal V(\bar\mu)$ and $(C_2)$. Let $x_\mu$ be the unique strong global solution of $S(A_\mu,u_0^\mu,v_0^\mu)$. Given $T>0$ with $\gamma T+\frac{T^2}{\alpha}\in[0,1)$, for all $\mu,\mu'$, $\|x_\mu-x_{\mu'}\|_\infty\leq\frac\alpha{\alpha-\alpha\gamma T-T^2}(\|u_0^\mu-u_0^{\mu'}\|+T\|v_0^\mu-v_0^{\mu'}\|+T^2\theta_1\|\mu-\mu'\|^{\theta_2}).\tag{25}$
items.proof: A strong solution satisfies $x(t)=u_0+tv_0+\int_0^t(s-t)[\gamma\dot x(s)+Ax(s)]ds\tag{26}$. Define $\Gamma_{A_\mu,u_0^\mu,v_0^\mu}(x)=u_0^\mu+tv_0^\mu+\int_0^t(s-t)[\gamma\dot x(s)+A_\mu x(s)]ds$. It has fixed point $x_\mu$ and is Lipschitz with constant $\gamma T+T^2/\alpha$. [Integrating $-\ddot x=\gamma\dot x+Ax$ twice gives the fixed-point identity.] [TODO: verify the stated Lipschitz estimate on $C([0,T];H)$, because the formula for $\Gamma$ contains $\dot x$; the natural domain must control derivatives.] Theorem 2.5 gives $\|x_\mu-x_{\mu'}\|_\infty\leq\frac\alpha{\alpha-\alpha\gamma T-T^2}\sup_x\|\Gamma_\mu(x)-\Gamma_{\mu'}(x)\|_\infty$. [For the operator term, $(C_2)$ gives $\|\int_0^t(s-t)[A_\mu x(s)-A_{\mu\prime}x(s)]ds\|\leq\theta_1\|\mu-\mu\prime\|^{\theta_2}\int_0^t(t-s)ds\leq T^2\theta_1\|\mu-\mu\prime\|^{\theta_2}$.] Estimate the latter by $\|u_0^\mu-u_0^{\mu'}\|+T\|v_0^\mu-v_0^{\mu'}\|+T^2\theta_1\|\mu-\mu'\|^{\theta_2}$ using $(C_2)$.
items.remark: [Prove hint: work on a differentiable/AC path space and bound the integral kernel carefully]

items.name: Remark 5.3
items.statement: If $\mu_n\to\bar\mu$, $x_n(t)=x_{\mu_n}(t)$, and $x(t)=x_{\bar\mu}(t)$, Theorem 5.2 (respectively Theorem 5.1) ensures $x_n$ converges uniformly almost everywhere on $[0,T]$ to $x$ whenever $u_0^n\to u_0$, $\dot u_0^n\to v_0$, the values belong to $B(0,\rho)$ (respectively $B(0,r)$), and $A_{\mu_n}$ converges to $A$ relative to $d_{\lambda,\rho}$ (respectively $D_r$).
items.remark: [Prove hint: preserve the paper notation and use the listed dependencies.]

items.name: Corollary 6.5
items.statement:
For each $\mu$, let $x_\mu$ be the unique solution of $DIN(\varphi,\mu)$. Assume $ eta\gamma>1$, each $\varphi(\cdot,\mu)$ is differentiable and $\delta_\mu$-strongly convex, and for given $r,T>0$, $x_\mu(t)\in B(0,r)$ for a.e. $t\in[0,T]$. Then $\|x_\mu(t)-x_{\mu'}(t)\|\leq e^{- eta\delta t}\sqrt{\|u_0^\mu-u_0^{\mu'}\|^2+\|v_0^\mu-v_0^{\mu'}\|^2}+ rac1\delta(1-e^{- eta\delta t})D_r(
abla\varphi_\mu,
abla\varphi_{\mu'})$. Moreover $x_\mu(t)$ strongly converges to the unique $ ar x_\mu$ of $(PM_\mu)$ and $\| ar x_\mu- ar x_{\mu'}\|\leq rac1\delta D_r(
abla\varphi_\mu,
abla\varphi_{\mu'})$.
items.remark: [Prove hint: preserve the paper notation and use the listed dependencies.]

items.name: Remark 7.2
items.statement: In $(C([0,T];H),\|\cdot\|_\infty)$, (3) becomes $\|x_\mu-x_{\mu'}\|_\infty\leq e^{mT}\sqrt{\|u_0^\mu-u_0^{\mu'}\|^2+\|v_0^\mu-v_0^{\mu'}\|^2}+\frac{\theta_1}{m}(e^{mT}-1)\|\mu-\mu'\|^{\theta_2}\tag{28}$, where $m=(1+2\gamma^2+\frac2{\alpha^2})^{1/2}$. For $\gamma T+T^2/\alpha\in[0,1)$, (25) refines (28) by sharp error bounds.
items.remark: [Prove hint: preserve the paper notation and use the listed dependencies.]

items.name: Theorem 7.4
items.statement: Assume for some $\alpha>0$ that $A_\mu$ is $\alpha$-cocoercive for each $\mu$, and let $x_\mu$ be the unique strong global solution of $S(A_\mu,u_0^\mu,v_0^\mu)$. Given $T>0$ with $\gamma T+\frac{T^2}{\alpha}\in[0,1)$, suppose for almost all $t\in[0,T]$ the function $\mu\mapsto A_\mu(x(t))$ is continuous in $\bar\mu$. Then $x_\mu$ converges uniformly to $x=x_{\bar\mu}$ as $\mu\to\bar\mu$, $u_0^\mu\to u_0$, and $v_0^\mu\to v_0$.
items.proof: At (27), take $\mu'=\bar\mu$. The estimate has the final term $\sup_x\sup_t\|\int_0^t(s-t)[A(x(s))-A_\mu(x(s))]ds\|$, which tends to zero uniformly in $t$ and $x$ by the continuity assumption and continuity under the integral sign. [TODO: verify: the stated assumption controls $A_\mu(x(t))$ only along the reference trajectory, whereas (27) contains a supremum over all $x\in C([0,T];H)$; uniform convergence on that larger class requires a stronger uniformity hypothesis.] The remaining initial-data terms tend to zero.
items.remark: [Prove hint: preserve the paper notation and use the listed dependencies.]

items.name: Definition 7.5
items.statement: A function $x\in C^1([0,T];H)$ is an $\varepsilon$-approximate solution to $S(A,u_0,v_0)$ iff it is an $\varepsilon$-fixed point of $\Gamma_{A,u_0,v_0}$, namely $x\in\varepsilon\text{-Fix}(\Gamma_{A,u_0,v_0}):=\{x\in C([0,T];H):\|x-\Gamma_{A,u_0,v_0}(x))\|\leq\varepsilon\}$. The set $\varepsilon$-Fix$(\Gamma_{A,u_0,v_0})$ is denoted $S^\varepsilon(A,u_0,v_0)$.
items.remark: [Prove hint: preserve the paper notation and use the listed dependencies.]

items.name: Theorem 7.8
items.statement: Assume the conditions of Theorem 7.1. For each $\mu$, let $x_\mu$ be the unique strong global solution of $S(A_\mu,u_0^\mu,v_0^\mu)$. For all $\varepsilon>0$ and all $\mu,\mu'$, $S^\varepsilon(\mu)$ and $S^\varepsilon(\mu')$ are nonempty and $h(S^\varepsilon(\mu),S^\varepsilon(\mu'))\leq\frac{\varepsilon\alpha}{\alpha-\alpha\gamma T-T^2}+\frac\alpha{\alpha-\alpha\gamma T-T^2}(\|u_0^\mu-u_0^{\mu'}\|+T\|v_0^\mu-v_0^{\mu'}\|+T^2\theta_1\|\mu-\mu'\|^{\theta_2}).\tag{29}$ In particular, this distance tends to $0$ when $\mu'\to\mu$, $u_0^{\mu'}\to u_0^\mu$, and $v_0^{\mu'}\to v_0^\mu$. When $\varepsilon\to0$, $S^\varepsilon(\mu)$ converges to $x_\mu$.
items.proof: Under Theorem 7.1, apply Theorem 2.4 to the contractions $\Gamma_{A_\mu,u_0^\mu,v_0^\mu}$ and $\Gamma_{A_{\mu'},u_0^{\mu'},v_0^{\mu'}}$. The supremum of their distance is bounded by $\|u_0^\mu-u_0^{\mu'}\|+T\|v_0^\mu-v_0^{\mu'}\|+T^2\theta_1\|\mu-\mu'\|^{\theta_2}$ via $(C_2)$, yielding (29). [The kernel estimate is the same as in Theorem 7.1: integrate $t-s$ over $[0,t]$ and bound it by $T^2$ (the sharper factor is $T^2/2$). The final convergence as $\varepsilon\to0$ additionally uses the cited approximate-fixed-point convergence result.]
items.remark: [Prove hint: Theorem 2.4 supplies the Hausdorff estimate; use ext_thm_6 for the final $\varepsilon\to0$ assertion]

items.name: Remark 7.9
items.statement: The exact estimate (25) of Theorem 7.1 is an immediate consequence of the approximate estimate (29) in Theorem 7.8 by passage to the limit as $\varepsilon\to0$.
items.remark: [Prove hint: preserve the paper notation and use the listed dependencies.]

external_theorems.name: Theorem 2.4
external_theorems.statement: Let $X$ be a metric space and let $T_1:X\rightrightarrows X$ and $T_2:X\rightrightarrows X$. Suppose that both $T_1$ and $T_2$ are Lipschitz continuous on $X$ with the same Lipschitz constant $\lambda\in[0,1)$. Then for every $\varepsilon>0$, $\varepsilon$-Fix$(T_i)\neq\emptyset$, $i=1,2$, and $h(\varepsilon\text{-Fix}(T_1),\varepsilon\text{-Fix}(T_2))\leq\frac\varepsilon{1-\lambda}+\frac1{1-\lambda}\sup_{x\in X}h(T_1(x),T_2(x)).$
external_theorems.proof: Cited from: M. Ait Mansour, M. A Bahraoui and A. El Bekkali, Metric regularity and Lyusternik-Graves theorem via approximate fixed points of set-valued map in noncomplete metric spaces, Set-Valued Var. Anal., 30 (2022), 233-256.
external_theorems.source: M. Ait Mansour, M. A Bahraoui and A. El Bekkali, Metric regularity and Lyusternik-Graves theorem via approximate fixed points of set-valued map in noncomplete metric spaces, Set-Valued Var. Anal., 30 (2022), 233-256.
external_theorems.remark: [Prove hint: preserve the paper notation and use the listed dependencies.]

external_theorems.name: Theorem 2.5 (Lim's Lemma)
external_theorems.statement: Let $X$ be a complete metric space and let $T_1,T_2$ be two maps from $X$ into the family of nonempty closed subsets of $X$. Suppose that both $T_1$ and $T_2$ are Lipschitz continuous on $X$ with the same Lipschitz constant $\lambda\in[0,1)$. Then $h(\operatorname{Fix}(T_1),\operatorname{Fix}(T_2))\leq\frac1{1-\lambda}\sup_{x\in X}h(T_1(x),T_2(x)).$
external_theorems.proof: Cited from: T.-C. Lim, On fixed-point stability for set-valued contractive mappings with applications to generalized differential equations, J. Math. Anal. Appl., 110 (1985), 436-441.
external_theorems.source: T.-C. Lim, On fixed-point stability for set-valued contractive mappings with applications to generalized differential equations, J. Math. Anal. Appl., 110 (1985), 436-441.

external_theorems.name: Lemma 2.6
external_theorems.statement: Let $T>0$, $a,b\in L^1(t_0,t_0+T;\mathbb R)$ with $b(t)\geq0$ for a.e. $t\in[t_0,t_0+T]$, $0\leq\alpha<1$, and let $w:[t_0,t_0+T]\to\mathbb R_+$ be absolutely continuous and satisfy $(1-\alpha)w'(t)\leq a(t)w(t)+b(t)w^\alpha(t)$ for a.e. $t\in[t_0,t_0+T]$. Then for all $t\in[t_0,t_0+T]$, $w^{1-\alpha}(t)\leq w^{1-\alpha}(t_0)e^{\int_{t_0}^t a(\tau)d\tau}+\int_{t_0}^t e^{\int_s^t a(\tau)d\tau}b(s)ds.$
external_theorems.proof: Cited from: R. E. Showalter, Monotone Operators in Banach Spaces and Nonlinear Partial Differential Equations, Math. Surveys Monogr., 49. American Mathematical Society, Providence, RI, 1997.
